title: A caller who can send requests to the temporal-proxy gRPC listener can obtain the static API key of an upstream whose…
description: A vulnerability in temporal-proxy versions 0.1.0 through 1.2.0 allows a caller who can send requests to the gRPC listener to obtain the static API key of an upstream service. This occurs because temporal-proxy does not validate the request namespace before using it to construct the upstream address, enabling a crafted namespace to redirect the proxy to a host controlled by the attacker. If the upstream verifies TLS using the system trust store without a literal server name, an attacker with a publicly trusted certificate can pass verification and receive the API key. The issue is fixed in versions 1.0.2, 1.1.2, and 1.2.1. Users should upgrade to these fixed versions and rotate any exposed API keys.
